q: We deliberately construct our dataset by injecting controlled ambiguities—Missing Goals (AG), Missing Premises (AP ), and Ambiguous Terminology (AT )—into the canonical HumanEval dataset.
r: EC6: tasks are HumanEval and LiveCodeBench problems (function-level), so not feature or project level; the contribution is a clarification benchmark, not an evaluation of building applications.

q: SlopCodeBench contains 36 language-agnostic problems spanning 196 checkpoints.
r: Include: iterative from-scratch application building with new cost and code-quality metrics (erosion, verbosity), so feature or project level and a method contribution.

q: RACE-Bench targets feature addition tasks with developer-provided tests.
r: Include: repository-level feature addition (not issue repair) and a new dual-track evaluation of patches and reasoning.

q: we introduce Vision2Web, a hierarchical benchmark that enables autonomous evaluation of multimodal coding agents on visual website development
r: Include: end-to-end website development benchmark from requirements, up to full-stack projects, with a new agent-verification method.

q: We use NITR to study coding agents and answer questions
r: EC4: preprint of the same Needle in the Repo benchmark; rayyan-800486847 is the published, more complete version.

q: REAP, a replicable methodology for curating production-derived benchmarks for AI coding agents
r: Include: the contribution is an evaluation method (benchmark curation with stability checks, repeated runs) on developer prompts, plus a context-file comparison.

q: evaluates agent performance across two dimensions: functional correctness
r: Include: sequential feature evolution of repositories, with new metrics for repository health (complexity, technical debt) beyond test passing.

q: CLI-Tool-Bench, the first structure-agnostic benchmark for evaluating end-to-end software generation from scratch
r: Include: project-level generation of CLI tools from scratch with a new black-box differential metric and cost analysis.

q: SWE-Bench Pro (Deng et al., 2025) requires agents to navigate large, real-world codebases and generate correct patches for GitHub issues
r: EC6: tasks are SWE-Bench Pro issue repair and text-to-SQL, both always excluded under EC6.

q: We introduce WebCompass, a comprehensive, multimodal benchmark that provides a unified lifecycle evaluation of web engineering capability
r: Include: includes end-to-end website generation from text, image or video, with a new Agent-as-a-Judge method.
